R4.2: BOTH OF THESE CLOSE BY CONSTRUCTION and are not evidence of anything. R_int is
ASSEMBLED as V_L + V_R, so sum-V is identically zero for any moment distribution however
wrong; both diagonals take H from the same Tneg, so sum-H is float noise. The same is true
of selfChecks.globalV_kip. They are asserted below only as model-consistency statements and
the row is now labelled that way. The load-bearing assertion is the cross-check below.
REACTION CROSS-CHECK (R4.2, statics.reactionCrossCheck). The support moments are re-derived by
Clapeyron's THREE-MOMENT equation — the force method: a different formulation and a different
solver from the direct-stiffness path, sharing no code with it — and the reactions are then
rebuilt from THOSE moments and compared with the shear-assembled reactions:
-> 4*M_1 = -w*L^2/2 -> M_1 = -w*L^2/8 = -11,676.210 k-in (sagging-positive) = exactly the
hogging moment the stiffness solve produced. Moment residual 0.
-> both equal the shear-assembled R exactly; residual 0 against tol 1e-8*W + 0.001 kip.
WHAT WOULD TRIP IT — this is why it is not a tautology. Change solveD's fixed-end moment from
w*L^2/12 to w*L^2/10, or the midspan-point FEM from P*L/8 to P*L/6, or flip a FEM sign, or use
kk = 1/L instead of 2/L. EVERY one of those leaves jointRes, globalV, globalM and the
interior-node sum-V/sum-H at EXACTLY zero — they are all derived from the same wrong moments —
while this residual moves by kips. WORKED PERTURBATION, FEM = w*L^2/10 instead of w*L^2/12:
for two equal spans the antisymmetric solve gives theta_1 = 0, theta_0 = F/(2*kk), hence
M_1 = -(kk*theta_0 + F) = -1.5*F. With the correct F = w*L^2/12 that is -w*L^2/8 = -11,676.210;
Three-moment end reaction: unchanged at 112.27125 k (its own load terms are correct).
Residual = 112.27125 - 104.78650 = 7.48475 kip against a 0.001 kip tolerance -> the engine
returns not_converged with code REACTION_CROSSCHECK. jointRes, globalV, globalM and the
interior-node sum-V/sum-H all remain exactly 0.0 under that same perturbation.
